chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah, from Isma'il ibn Abi Ziyad, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, from his father, from 'Ali عليه السلام, who said:
An eye is not assessed on a cloudy day.

key_terms.تُقَاسُ: is measured or assessed in a legal evaluative context
key_terms.عَيْنٌ: an eye, referring to the bodily organ in injury law
key_terms.غَيْمٍ: cloudiness or overcast weather, a condition affecting accurate examination
key_terms.يَوْمِ: day, indicating the time of assessment

ai.seo_question: Why should an injured eye not be assessed on a cloudy day in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling in the context of bodily injury assessment. It states that an eye should not be evaluated on a cloudy day, indicating that proper assessment depends on conditions that allow accurate judgment.
